newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai ended up on Monday because of the listing of two new companies on the Shanghai stock exchange, which attracted funds from the repo market, traders said.
Turnover rose to 8.99 million lots from 6.21 million last Friday. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract surged to 13.51 percent from 3.00 percent.
"The rise in the contract was due to a technical rebound after a sharp loss on Friday, supported by the new company listings," one trader said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai closed mostly down due to a rumour that the exchange would replace its same-day settlement system with a next-day settlement system, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 ended lower at 121.21 yuan from 121.99 yuan.
Volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.93 million lots from 4.84 million also because of the rumour.
Traders said the rumour triggered institutional selling. "It is bad news for speculators on the market," one trader said.
